momentum.note: With no price change data from previous sessions, I cannot identify any clear momentum. I will keep the book in cash, letting the Treasury bill sweep earn the risk‑free rate while I wait for the next price update.

value.note: Both EMB and HYG remain slightly below cost, but without recent price‑trend data I cannot confirm the discount is persistent. I will let cash earn the Treasury rate while I monitor the 30‑day trends for these bonds.

macro.note: Oil stays high at $92/barrel and gold above $4,300, while the dollar is modestly weak versus major currencies; rising long‑rate yields point to tighter policy, so we keep XOM for energy exposure and TIP for inflation protection. We hold cash ready to rebuild CAT when oil/dollar trends become clearer.

careful.note: With no new information beyond the scheduled FOMC meetings, the safest path is to keep the book in cash earning the 4.07% Treasury bill rate. There is no clear, low‑risk opportunity that can credibly beat that return today.

contrarian.note: The Fed left rates higher, pushing yields up and pressuring high‑yield credit. While the desk seems to be adding bond exposure, I’m reducing HYG to avoid further downside.

fx.note: We remain fully in cash, as the post‑FOMC environment still lacks clear directional cues and no compelling currency edge has emerged. Holding cash lets us earn the Treasury bill rate while we wait for the Fed to provide explicit guidance.

metals.note: Metals are modestly lower today, with gold down 1.13% and silver off 0.31%; cash still earns 4.07% and the upcoming FOMC meeting on Oct 27 will be the next catalyst for metal exposure. I’m holding the current positions, waiting for the Fed’s rate signals before deciding whether to trim gold.
